meta_title: Not a BlueCart Alternative: Keep BlueCart, Add Voice Ordering
meta_desc: Keep the BlueCart listing that finds new kitchens, and give your regulars a reorder they speak into an app. A BlueCart alternative that removes nothing.

hero.h1: Not A BlueCart Alternative: Reorders For Your Regulars
hero.lead: Keep winning new accounts on the marketplace and give the ones you already supply a faster reorder. VoiceOrder Solutions lives next to BlueCart: kitchens say what they are short of into our app, approve the list and send it, priced off your own guide.

problem.h2: When an alternative to BlueCart starts to look tempting
problem.lead: BlueCart sells reach: it helps you find new customers. You join their marketplace, get listed in what they call the "endless aisle", and restaurants across their network can see you. That is worth keeping for a supplier chasing new accounts. Once an account is yours, though, the weekly reorder is a different job, and that is usually when a BlueCart competitor gets a look.

cards.h3: The reorder still comes by phone
cards.body: Plenty of accounts never order online at all. They call at seven in the morning or after close, and someone at your end writes each order up.

cards.h3: Online ordering helps the ones who log in
cards.body: BlueCart presents its Order Management Solution as a replacement for phone and email ordering. For buyers who use it, it does replace them. The kitchens who prefer talking to logging in are the gap.

cards.h3: Leaving would cost you new customers
cards.body: Coming off the marketplace would give up the new kitchens it brings in, and the regulars on the phone would still be on the phone. That is why a BlueCart alternative that takes the listing down is the wrong fix here.

cards.h2: BlueCart finds the account, voice adds a quicker reorder
cards.lead: VoiceOrder Solutions is not a BlueCart replacement, because it cannot do the thing BlueCart is for. It adds on, so you can use it and stay listed on the marketplace.

items.h3: Meet them on BlueCart, make reordering quick
items.body: A marketplace is a good way to meet an account you had no route to. Once they buy from you regularly, some will want a quicker way to reorder than logging in, and our app gives them one while the listing keeps working.

items.h3: Let each account order the way it likes
items.body: Kitchens happy ordering through BlueCart can keep doing it. Regulars who would still rather call get an app that turns what they say into a list they check.

items.h3: Our orders land where you choose
items.body: Ours show up in whichever system you picked, by EDI, through the API or in QuickBooks, or as an email to your desk. Nothing about your BlueCart dashboard changes.

midcta.h3: See a regular's reorder go from voice to your desk
midcta.body: Twenty minutes. One account, a single spoken order from a sample guide, signed off before it sends.

faq.h2: What distributors on BlueCart ask us

items.q: Is a BlueCart alternative the only way to add spoken orders?
items.a: No, and the listing never has to come down. VoiceOrder Solutions adds an app where the accounts on your books say what they need and approve it, while BlueCart goes on bringing in kitchens that are new to you. Nothing gets turned off.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than BlueCart?
items.a: At finding new customers, no, and it is not a close call. That is what BlueCart sells, and we offer nothing like it. We help with the repeat order from an account already on your books: only your products, at your prices, approved by your customer. People who search for a BlueCart alternative often want help with repeat orders, not a way to stop meeting new kitchens.

items.q: Are VoiceOrder Solutions and BlueCart connected?
items.a: No. The two products are not linked, and neither supports the other. Each delivers its orders into your own system independently, ours as an email with a file attached, over EDI or the API, or into QuickBooks.

items.q: Won't our accounts be ordering in two places?
items.a: Some may, and that can be fine. A kitchen you met on the marketplace can keep buying there. Offer our app to the regulars who still call your desk, since a spoken reorder from your own guide is where it saves the most time. Calls you go on taking get no order number from us; that only comes with orders sent through the app.

items.q: How do our prices appear in your app?
items.a: Each account sees its own guide, priced the way you set it. BlueCart's Pricing Insights, which labels products as great, good or fair value, carries on for your marketplace listing.

items.q: How fast can accounts begin ordering?
items.a: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, with a first order usually in on the same day. BlueCart says theirs can be live within days too, and since the listing stays up, there is nothing to schedule around.
Neither of us publishes a figure. Theirs follows a demo; ours comes as a quote once we have talked. With the listing kept, the only new cost is the voice reorder, and a quote shows what that is.

items.q: Where do the BlueCart details on this page come from?
items.a: Everything here came from bluecart.com, read 10 October 2026: the marketplace positioning off the headline, the Pricing Insights and endless aisle descriptions off their product list, and the setup line off their FAQ. We have left their transaction and funding figures alone, because those are theirs. If something there is out of date now, we will fix it.

mainCta.h2: Keep the listing. Get regulars' reorders off the phone.
mainCta.body: Twenty minutes, one order priced from a guide, and approved before it sends.
